transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-03-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Rivers (Nova CTO), Jenna Park (Nova Lead ML Eng), Omar Santos (Nova SRE)

Summary:
Quick integration discovery: customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for model inference. Focus areas: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex compatibility, gateway/proxy for internal routing, rate limits and quotas, observability hooks and tracing, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Agreed next steps and artifacts to share.

Topics:
- SDKs and examples (Python/TS)
- LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors
- Gateway/proxy pattern and allowed egress
- Rate limiting, per-tenant quotas, burst policies
- Observability: traces, per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdowns
- Security: VPC, SAML/SSO, KMS, audit logs

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh really quick intro, I'm alex i'm the account exec on this one, with priya our se, and then we have mark jenn and omar from nova. how's everyone doing?
00:08 Mark Rivers: good thanks, thanks for doing this, we've been looking at redwood and a couple others, wanted to make sure integration story fits our stack.
00:14 Priya Nair: awesome, quick agenda, we'll run through SDKs, langchain/llamaindex, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits and observability, then q&a and next steps. sound good?
00:23 Jenna Park: sounds great. by way of context, we're building a multi-tenant document QA product that will call LLMs for embeddings and chat, currently prototype on openai but cost + latency at scale are concerns.
00:36 Omar Santos: and from infra side, we need VPC peering or dedicated private deployment, egress allowlist, and we operate in AWS us-east-1 for now.
00:45 Alex Martinez: got it. can you share rough traffic profile — rps, latency targets?
00:52 Jenna Park: sure, right now peak is ~150 RPS across tenants, average prompt size 600 tokens, target p99 latency for chat~500ms, embeddings under 200ms if possible.
01:05 Priya Nair: OK that helps a lot. hosted can be a good quick start but if p99 500ms is strict we usually recommend dedicated or private with pinned capacity. we also do prefix caching and kv cache to help latency on repeated prompts.
01:20 Mark Rivers: when you say kv cache is that the kv cache in the model runtime? sometimes vendors call different things.
01:28 Priya Nair: yeah it's our KV cache layer - stores key/value decoder states, helps with long conversations and shorter tail latency. sometimes we call it K V cache in docs, sorry for inconsistency.
01:36 Jenna Park: cool. on integration, how mature are your SDKs? we use python and node, and our orchestration is langchain-based.
01:44 Alex Martinez: we have official SDKs in python and typescript, examples for direct calls, streaming, and embeddings. also prebuilt connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex — we have example notebooks.
01:54 Priya Nair: i'll drop a link after the call — integration guide + langchain/llamaindex snippets, small notebook showing streaming + function call pattern.
02:03 Jenna Park: you said llamaindex?
02:05 Priya Nair: sorry — llamaindex. we also show how to wire Redwood as a llm provider in LangChain using the chain-of-thought wrappers.
02:18 Mark Rivers: do you provide cross-tenant rate limits and per-API-key quotas? we need isolation by customer and fairshare.
02:27 Priya Nair: yes, rate limits can be applied at route, api-key, and tenant level. quotas are configurable per account with alerts and soft throttling. for dedicated customers you can set stricter network-level policies.
02:40 Omar Santos: what's the behavior when the quota is hit? do you return 429s? exponential backoff? any queueing?
02:47 Alex Martinez: default is 429 with a Retry-After header, but we support a burst/queue window on Dedicated where requests can be queued for short periods; also you can wire fallback routes to cheaper model variants.
02:59 Jenna Park: fallback to smaller models might be acceptable for non-critical flows. what about a gateway/proxy — we want to run a local gateway so internal services talk to local proxy and it forwards to redwood with egress controls. any best practices?
03:12 Priya Nair: common pattern is a lightweight sidecar or API gateway in your VPC that handles authentication, per-tenant routing, request shaping, and retry logic. we provide health checks and a manifest for recommended headers and timeouts.
03:26 Alex Martinez: for private deployments we can also host the gateway within your VPC so traffic never leaves; Hosted customers often use a proxy with allowlisted egress IPs.
03:36 Omar Santos: allowlist ips — can you share the list? and what's the frequency of ip changes?
03:41 Priya Nair: we'll send a stable block for Hosted, changes happen rarely but we publish a notice. for Dedicated/Private you control the egress. we'll include IPs in the security pack.
03:53 Mark Rivers: observability — what hooks do we get? we need traces, token-level cost, per-route latency, and integration to our datadog/jaeger.
04:02 Priya Nair: we emit structured logs, metrics (Prometheus style), and distributed traces compatible with OpenTelemetry. token-level cost breakdowns and per-model dashboards are available in Redwood Console, plus webhook alerts for regressions.
04:18 Jenna Park: is there correlation ids we pass through? we need to connect request traces from our app to redwood traces.
04:24 Priya Nair: yes, pass X-Request-Id and we will return it in logs and traces. we also support custom metadata fields that show up in the console.
04:33 Mark Rivers: what about SSO / RBAC / audit logs — auditors will want proof for compliance.
04:39 Alex Martinez: we support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, role-based access, and audit logs retained per contract terms. SOC 2 docs available.
04:48 Jenna Park: KMS? we have keys in our AWS KMS and want BYOK for model payload encryption at rest.
04:55 Priya Nair: BYOK via customer-managed KMS is supported for Private, and for Dedicated we offer KMS integrations — details in security pack we'll share.
05:04 Omar Santos: latency question — for chat flow with streaming, what are token emission latencies? we've seen variability with some runtimes.
05:12 Priya Nair: on optimized runtimes we typically see first token under 200-300ms depending on model size and prompt, then steady per-token times. Dedicated GPUs with optimized kernels reduce variance; we can run benchmarks with your sample prompts.
05:25 Jenna Park: can we run a pilot benchmark? we can share a telemetry-free sample dataset.
05:30 Alex Martinez: absolutely. typical path is 2-week pilot on Dedicated or Hosted with synthetic traffic and later move to a private deployment if needed.
05:38 Mark Rivers: pricing — skimming costs on the call is fine but we'll need banded pricing for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
05:44 Alex Martinez: i'll send a preliminary pricing band; dedicated pricing includes reserved capacity + overage, private is by license + infra.
05:50 Jenna Park: latency SLOs matter for our product, can you commit to p99 numbers?
05:55 Priya Nair: SLA-backed latency targets exist for Dedicated at contract levels; for Hosted we provide performance profiles per model and recommend dedicated if tight p99s are required.
06:05 Omar Santos: anything around data residency? some customers require EU only.
06:09 Priya Nair: we have regions in NA and EU, and Private can be deployed on-prem or in your region for residency.
06:17 Mark Rivers: what are gotchas with langchain integrations — we use chains, memory, retrievers.
06:23 Priya Nair: main things are streaming + function calls with LangChain's callback handlers; we provide a LangChain agent wrapper and LlamaIndex connector; watch for tokenization differences and chunk sizes for retrievers. we also provide prompt templates and eval harness examples.
06:38 Jenna Park: perfect. can you also share security questionnaire answers and SOC2?
06:42 Alex Martinez: yes we'll send the security pack and the network allowlist IPs.
06:46 Mark Rivers: ok next steps — a deep technical session with priya to discuss private deployment and gateway, plus pilot pricing and samples.
06:54 Alex Martinez: great, i'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifacts. thanks everyone.
06:58 Mark Rivers: thanks all.
07:00 End of recording.
